result:
**Verdict: PASS.** I reviewed DG1 candidate `sha256:24eb3779…b08e` (freeze commit `5f83a336`). All five fixes assigned to me hold up. I raised two new findings, both Low and not mandatory violations, so they don't block the gate.

**Identity:** HEAD was `d3fcb89`, not the freeze commit, but it sits one commit after `5f83a336` and adds only metadata excluded from the candidate. The candidate ID recomputed to the same value in the real repo and in a clone checked out at the freeze commit. I didn't author any of the code under review and didn't read any other reviewer's round-5 record. The orchestrator committed the domain reviewer's record while I was running; I didn't open it.

**Fixes verified (all now CLOSED_VERIFIED):**
- **F-DG1-122 (Medium):** the installer acceptance test no longer deletes a developer's files. I planted five files, including `.vscode/tasks.json` and `CLAUDE.local.md`, ran the suite, and all five came back byte-identical. When I swapped in a fake installer that doesn't sandbox anything, the AC-8 check fails as it should and removes only files it created itself.
- **F-DG1-123 (Low):** node_modules is copied back only to the real workspace members; a stray `package.json` outside the workspace no longer gets one. When I forced the copy or the delete to fail, the install exits 1 with an error message. `create` and `frozen` still populate every member.
- **F-DG1-124 (Low):** both required plants (`f["constr"+"uctor"]` and `Reflect.get(fn,"constructor")`) are flagged, and as real files in the module tree they make `architecture.test.ts` fail. The real module tree passes 74/74 with no findings. The refactored module code behaves the same, and the integration suite covers it.
- **F-DG1-204:** `generate-sbom --check` passes on the committed tree.
- **F-DG1-205:** the three `ci.yml` copies are byte-identical.

**New findings:**
- **F-DG1-125 (Low):** the module lint misses the native loaders `binding` and `dlopen` when `process` is reached through `import … from "node:process"`. With that in a module file, `architecture.test.ts` stays green, and I confirmed both functions are live in Node 22. Neither is a JavaScript module loader, so this is a gap in the lint's own claim rather than a real boundary escape. Owner: backend-workflow-engineer.
- **F-DG1-126 (Low):** the installer's workspace-member resolver (`install-sandbox.sh:154-168`) treats every list item in `pnpm-workspace.yaml` as a member pattern and ignores `!` exclusions. In a test workspace, an excluded directory and an unrelated settings entry both received node_modules planted by a dependency. The committed workspace file isn't affected; this only matters if someone later adds such entries. Owner: delivery-orchestrator.

**Checks:**

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| typecheck, build, lint, `openapi:lint`, `check:no-cdn`, `format:check` | all exit 0 |
| Unit tests | 267/267 |
| Integration, on a throwaway PostgreSQL 16 (port 5497), run twice | 200/200 both times |
| Gate and agent tooling tests | 105/105 |
| Deploy script tests | 59/59 |
| SBOM check | pass |
| DG0 historical validation | pass |
| Evidence cited by the 8 assigned requirements | 82 paths, none missing |
| Installer acceptance suite | 12/13 here; AC-1 (effect) BLOCKED |

AC-1 (effect) needs the npm registry, which my sandbox can't reach. An offline version with the unchanged installer passes, and the orchestrator's committed 13/13 run is on file.

**Observations, not raised as findings:**
- If the sandbox were already broken, AC-8's probe would overwrite an existing `apps/api/CLAUDE.md`; the test would still report FAIL in that case.
- The lint scans only `.ts`/`.tsx` files. A `.js`/`.mjs` file in `src/modules` wouldn't make it into the production build.

The JSON record (validated against the gate schemas), sidecars and narrative are in `docs/delivery/reviews/DG1/round-5/code-security-reviewer.*`. Evidence and reproduction scripts are in `docs/delivery/test-evidence/DG1/code-security/round-5/`. I've deleted the throwaway clones and the store copy.
